summary: John Griffiths (1837–1918) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Royal College of Art and held a post at the Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy School of Art from circa 1865 to 1895.
John H. Berthrong works in Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He completed graduate studies under Alfonso Verdu and held a post at Boston University, attested in 1996.

John Henry Hutton (1885–1968) was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Chigwell School (~1898–1904) and Worcester College, Oxford (~1904–1908), later serving in the Indian Civil Service (~1909–1935).

Classicist John Henry Wright studied at Dartmouth and Leipzig under Georg Curtius. He taught at Ohio State (1873–1876), Dartmouth (1878–1886), and Johns Hopkins (1886), before serving as professor at Harvard (~1887–1908) and Athens (1906–1907).

John Herbert Harington (1765–1828) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as secretary (1790) and president (1825–1828) of The Asiatic Society, and was an honorary professor at Fort William College (~1801–1805).
John Hope (1725–1786) studied at the University of Edinburgh circa 1740–1750. He subsequently held a post at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1761 to 1786.

Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar John Hurrell Crook studied at Southampton and Cambridge under Robert Hinde and William Homan Thorpe, and with Sheng Yen. He taught at Bristol (~1963–1993) and founded the Western Chan Fellowship in 1997.

John J. Holder works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied under Harry Krebs. He held a visiting research post at the University of Oxford and posts at St. Norbert College (attested in 2006 and 2018).

John J. Makransky studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Lobsang Tendzin, and other teachers. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he held posts at Boston College, CIHTS, and Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

John James Jones (1892–1957) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Aberystwyth University (~1912–1919) and served as Deputy-Keeper in the Department of Printed Books at the National Library of Wales (~1926–1957).

John Jorgensen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He has held posts as a researcher at the Australian National University, taught Japanese Studies at Griffith University, and served at La Trobe University (attested 2019).

John Kieschnick is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held a post at the University of Bristol (~2005–2011) and was appointed Robert H. N. Ho Family Foundation Professor of Buddhist Studies at Stanford University in ~2011.

Philosopher John Lane Bell studied at Lick-Wilmerding High School and the University of Oxford (~1963–1968). He held positions at the London School of Economics (~1968–1989), the University of Western Ontario (~1989), and the National University of Singapore.
John Leyden (1775–1811) worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Henry Thomas Colebrooke (~1803–1811) and served as assistant secretary and secretary at The Asiatic Society (~1809–1811).

John Lockwood Kipling studied at Woodhouse Grove School and worked in Indology and archaeology. He taught at the Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy School of Art (~1865–1875) and served as Principal of the National College of Arts (1875–1893).

John M. Koller, working in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies, studied at the East-West Center under Shri Krishna Saksena, Charles Alexander Moore, and George T. Artola. He held a professorship at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (attested 1988, 1999).

John M. Rosenfield studied at UT Austin, SMU, UC Berkeley, Iowa, and Harvard under Benjamin Rowland. Specializing in art history and Japanology, he taught at Iowa, UCLA, and served as professor and curator at Harvard (1965–1991).

John Marshall studied at Cambridge and the British School at Athens under Arthur Evans. An archaeologist and Indologist, he served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1902–1931) and was a Fellow at King's College, Cambridge (~1927–1958).

John Muir (1810–1882) studied at Glasgow, Bonn, and East India Company College (~1826–1828). He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1828–1853), was principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1844), and held posts at the University of Edinburgh.
John Myrdhin Reynolds is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak (~1971), Dudjom Rinpoche (~1971–1987), and Namkhai Norbu (~1979).
